stimulus.contextLine: Listen to part of a talk in a biology class.

transcript.speaker: Professor
transcript.text: Today we look at mitochondria. You probably know them as the power plants of the cell. But they have a second job: they help remove damaged cells. When a cell is badly damaged, mitochondria send signals that start its breakdown.

items.prompt: What is the talk mainly about?

options.rationale: A is wrong: cell division is not discussed.
B is right: energy and removing damaged cells.
C is wrong: sugar is not mentioned.
D is wrong: the talk is about cells, not plants.

explanation.summary: The professor describes the power-plant role and a second job of mitochondria.

items.prompt: What is the professor’s point about mitochondria?

options.text: They produce energy faster than any other part
options.rationale: A is wrong: speed is not compared.

options.text: They also help remove damaged cells
options.rationale: B is right: the second job.

options.text: They are found only in animals
options.rationale: C is wrong: animals are not mentioned.
D is wrong: heat is not mentioned.

explanation.summary: “They have a second job: they help remove damaged cells.”

items.prompt: What happens when a cell is badly damaged?

options.rationale: A is wrong: they do not repair it.
B is right: they start its breakdown.
C is wrong: energy is not mentioned here.
D is wrong: division is not mentioned.

explanation.summary: Mitochondria send signals that start the breakdown of the cell.
